title: Ember and Veil
premise: Jonah Joubert, a cartographer exiled to a valley where magic cannot follow, has spent his life mapping realms he can never enter. When a child named Sef arrives at his door speaking a language older than any kingdom, Jonah discovers the child is a living fragment of Veylmark — a country erased from existence by a jealous empire, whose people survive only as memories. The two are pulled into the fading country itself, where they must find the Last Door before Veylmark's final memory dissolves and takes Sef with it. Along the way Jonah learns he is heir to the cartographer's guild that helped erase Veylmark, and must choose between restoring his family's name and sacrificing his own memories of the journey. In the end, Jonah gives up his recollection of Sef and their love to anchor the country back into the world; Sef survives, and years later finds Jonah in the valley with a map drawn in a hand he doesn't remember but trusts.
about_author: W. M. Ravensworth is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing maps of places that no longer appear on any modern atlas. They write fantasy about borders, both real and imagined, from a house at the edge of a valley much like Jonah's.

chapters.title: The Valley That Refuses
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. We meet him in the magicless valley, meticulously mapping impossible realms he'll never see, haunted by why he was sent here. A storm knocks a half-drowned child against his door. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness cracked open by sudden responsibility.

chapters.title: A Language Older Than Kingdoms
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The child, Sef, speaks an unrecorded tongue; Jonah recognizes its structure from forbidden guild fragments. Sef draws a coastline Jonah has only ever dreamed. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread as Jonah realizes the child shouldn't exist.

chapters.title: What the Guild Buried
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Raiding his inherited trunk of guild papers, Jonah finds his father's signature on the Edict of Unmapping — the document that erased Veylmark. Emotional beat: betrayal; inheritance revealed as complicity.

chapters.title: The Door in the Fogline
chapters.summary: Sef's POV, rendered in strange, sensory prose. Sef feels the erased country pulling them home and leads Jonah past the valley's edge where magic cannot follow. Emotional beat: fear and trust entwined as they cross together.

chapters.title: Veylmark, Half-Remembered
chapters.summary: Dual POV. They enter a country built of collective memory: streets solid where remembered, mist where forgotten. Sef grows stronger here; Jonah begins to fade. Emotional beat: awe shadowed by mortality.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Daughter
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. A memory-woman who guards the archive of everything Veylmark was, she tests Jonah and names him heir to the guild that doomed her home. Emotional beat: hostility laced with reluctant recognition of shared grief.

chapters.title: Lessons in Fading
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Ilsa teaches him how erasure works: every unmapped thing loses a memory daily. Sef is the last new memory Veylmark will ever make. Emotional beat: tenderness between Jonah and Sef deepening under a countdown.

chapters.title: The Empire's Surveyors
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Imperial surveyors still patrol the fogline, re-erasing anything that regains form. The party is ambushed; Ilsa burns a precious memory to save them. Emotional beat: first true loss, and rage.

chapters.title: The Road That Forgets Itself
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Traveling toward the capital, the road loops and renames itself; Jonah's cartographer instincts become survival skills. He and Sef share stories to keep each other anchored. Emotional beat: intimacy forged through mutual remembering.

chapters.title: The City of Second Names
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The ruined capital holds citizens who survived erasure by taking false identities. Some welcome Sef as hope; others want to use the child as fuel for their own permanence. Emotional beat: hope complicated by desperation.

chapters.title: The Council of What Remains
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The remnant council reveals the Last Door can reopen Veylmark but demands a life's worth of memory as the key. Jonah conceals that his guild blood makes his memories uniquely potent. Emotional beat: guilt and secrecy.

chapters.title: Night of Lanterns
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The city holds one last festival, lighting lanterns for things already forgotten. Sef dances with Jonah and confesses fear not of dying but of being unloved. Emotional beat: love declared plainly, on borrowed time.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Archive
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. A council faction steals Sef to power their own escape through the Door, stranding everyone else. Ilsa discovers Jonah's hidden heritage and accuses him of planning the same theft. Emotional beat: shattered alliances.

chapters.title: The Guild's True Map
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. To track Sef, Jonah deciphers his father's master map and finds it isn't a record of erasure but instructions for reversal — his father's secret repentance. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Through the Hollow Hills
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Imprisoned beneath the hills, Sef befriends a jailer-memory and learns the faction plans to open the Door alone, which will consume Sef entirely. Emotional beat: terror met with stubborn courage.

chapters.title: The Rescue That Costs
chapters.summary: Jonah and Ilsa's alternating POV. They assault the hollows; Ilsa spends her final memories holding the collapsing passage open, becoming mist in Jonah's arms. Emotional beat: sacrifice, and forgiveness offered too late to say aloud.

chapters.title: The Last Door
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. At the Door, the faction leader forces a confrontation; the Door opens only for willing memory freely given. Jonah realizes his guild-born memories could restore Veylmark whole — including Sef. Emotional beat: the choice crystallizing.

chapters.title: What Jonah Gives
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, intimate and slow. He offers every memory of Veylmark, Sef, and the road — the price of anchoring the country back into the world. Sef begs him not to; he does it anyway, kissing the child's brow as the world rewrites. Emotional beat: devastating, loving surrender.

chapters.title: A Country Returns
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Veylmark floods back into being — rivers, bells, names — as Sef wakes in a real bed in a real nation, the last fragment made whole. But Jonah is gone, and cannot remember why his heart aches. Emotional beat: triumph braided with loss.

chapters.title: The Valley Without Him
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Back in the valley with no memory of the journey, Jonah finds gaps in his journals and a finished map of a country he's never heard of, drawn in his hand. Emotional beat: hollow yearning without a name.

chapters.title: Ember
chapters.summary: Sef's POV, years later. Now grown and Veylmark's youngest surveyor, Sef carries the map Jonah once drew and walks the fogline into the magicless valley, following the ember of something remembered. Emotional beat: patient, hopeful devotion.

chapters.title: Veil
chapters.summary: Alternating final POV. Sef knocks on Jonah's door again, mirroring chapter one. Jonah doesn't know the visitor, yet offers shelter instinctively; when Sef says 'you drew me home,' something in him answers. Emotional beat: love outlasting memory — a beginning disguised as a return.
